subject: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc23 legacy TensorRT backend removal

selection.reason: TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc23 removes the legacy TensorRT engine build and execution contract in favor of a sole PyTorch backend. Exact tag, merge ancestry, migration documentation, deleted source paths and a public package artifact make the boundary verifiable, while teams running NVIDIA inference stacks need concrete CI/CD, provenance and canary decisions.

signals.note: Reviewed recent OpenAI release notes, Anthropic newsroom and Google AI and developer announcement surfaces. Search result snippets were used only for discovery; no unverified snippet became article evidence, and no newer lab release provided a stronger exact-artifact decision boundary than the selected candidate.

Queried official release surfaces for Transformers, PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, TensorRT-LLM, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google GenAI SDKs. The selected candidate was then verified against NVIDIA's exact tag, merged PRs, immutable documentation and PyPI artifact rather than the discovery output.

Opened current public X profile surfaces for registered infrastructure, hardware and evaluation researchers including Tri Dao, Tim Dettmers, Jim Fan and Sayash Kapoor. The pages exposed no post text through the unauthenticated interface, and search found no timely material signal that could be upgraded to a primary artifact; X supplied no article fact or source.

alternatives.subject: TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc23 legacy TensorRT backend removal
alternatives.reason: The release changes build, deployment and artifact-provenance contracts for NVIDIA inference teams and exposes exact source, migration docs, package metadata and bounded known issues.

alternatives.subject: llama.cpp b10235 Metal SILU_BACK and F16 binary operations
alternatives.reason: The same-day commits and binary artifacts are exact, but the two Metal operator additions are narrow and do not establish a sufficiently broad software deployment decision for this edition.

alternatives.reason: The release and exact commits are public, but the environment resource and Maps type additions have a smaller cross-team deployment impact than the TensorRT-LLM backend removal.

conflicts: NVIDIA and TensorRT-LLM contributors describe their own release, migration contract, implementation, package and known issues.
GitHub and PyPI host the public source and package records used to inspect artifact identity.
No advance access, vendor account, paid subscription, credits, hardware, sponsorship, advertising relationship, NDA or embargo was provided.

claims.claim: TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc23 resolves to commit d41ab33df16740e18e8ef9c8735dad4efc46afd5, and merge commits for the legacy backend, TensorRT SDK image path, tests/examples/CI and legacy Python documentation removal are ancestors of that tag.
claims.method: Resolved refs/tags/v1.3.0rc23 through the GitHub API to d41ab33df16740e18e8ef9c8735dad4efc46afd5; inspected PRs #16369, #16608, #16610 and #16612; compared merge commits c77bc6ed6b044f48c174e786b5a5f7fafeee1728, 56f28cd7af7fa07a8c92bf215627cc5e0f6018b9, f9c253ed3244d25eb2833ce360fd054941e02f3d and 3c07ada3c5af0fd31c6c91628392330ba38cc99a to the tag. Each comparison was ahead with behind_by 0.

sources.limitations: Maintainer-authored notes select and characterize changes and do not independently validate runtime behavior.
The Git tag fixes repository identity but does not identify every NGC image or NVIDIA-index wheel.
The PR is project-authored and its full test suite was not rerun by the editorial run.

limitations: No GPU runtime, wheel or container was executed.
A downstream distributor may carry a patch set different from the official tag.
GitHub compare establishes ancestry, not behavioral correctness.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA maintainers publish the release and removal commits being evaluated.
recheck_triggers: The release is yanked or its tag changes
A follow-up RC restores or replaces a removed interface
NVIDIA publishes a correction to the migration contract

claims.claim: In v1.3.0rc23 the TensorRT engine backend is removed, PyTorch is the sole execution backend, backend=tensorrt raises ValueError, and trtllm-build, trtllm-refit, trtllm-prune, per-model checkpoint conversion and the tensorrt pip dependency are removed.
claims.method: Downloaded the immutable migration guide at tag d41ab33df16740e18e8ef9c8735dad4efc46afd5 and matched its replacement table against PR #16369's 581-file removal, including FindTensorRT.cmake, rawEngine.h, trtGptModel paths and C++ benchmarks, plus PR #16610's test/example/CI removal.

sources.limitations: The guide defines supported migration behavior but does not measure compatibility or performance for a specific deployment.

sources.version: merge commit c77bc6ed6b044f48c174e786b5a5f7fafeee1728; 581 files; 2,697 additions; 78,984 deletions
sources.limitations: File deletion confirms implementation removal but does not enumerate downstream scripts outside the repository.
Removal of tests and examples does not prove every external integration has a direct replacement.

limitations: TensorRT-LLM still contains CUDA kernels, C++ executor code and NVIDIA-specific optimizations.
Triton Inference Server integration is distinct from the removed TensorRT engine backend.
AutoDeploy remains available on the PyTorch backend.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA defines and documents its own supported backend contract.
recheck_triggers: A stable 1.3 release changes the migration table
A compatibility layer for a removed command is published
Downstream tools report an undocumented retained TensorRT engine path

claims.claim: The public PyPI record for tensorrt_llm 1.3.0rc23 exposes a 215,516-byte sdist with SHA-256 07b5714cc51ff7f841cdf2f9fc2f71b68391e1480b1cf4d11ad7fbcac63f0b91; its archive contains wheel-stub configuration pointing to https://pypi.nvidia.com/ rather than the project runtime source.
claims.method: Queried the PyPI JSON endpoint, downloaded tensorrt_llm-1.3.0rc23.tar.gz, matched its 215,516-byte size and SHA-256, listed all four payload files and inspected pyproject.toml and PKG-INFO without executing the package.

sources.owner: Python Package Index / NVIDIA package publisher
sources.limitations: The public sdist delegates wheel acquisition to an NVIDIA index, whose final artifact was not downloaded.
The guide describes supported installation paths but actual index availability, regional access and resolver output can change.
The PR removes TensorRT SDK installation from project images but does not identify every third-party base image.

limitations: The NVIDIA-index wheel and NGC container were not downloaded, hashed or executed.
Package index contents can change after the observation time.
Dependency resolution behavior depends on pip configuration and the base environment.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA controls the delegated package index and publishes the installation guidance.
recheck_triggers: The PyPI file list, size, hash or yanked state changes
NVIDIA publishes signed wheel or container manifests
The wheel-stub index or dependency contract changes

claims.claim: The v1.3.0rc23 release note reports bounded known issues including DeepSeek hangs or crashes on specified GB300 and scheduler configurations, Qwen MoE multi-LoRA sampling failure, Gemma3 FP8 CUDA graph capture failure and Qwen3.5 BF16 OOM on A100 TP1.
claims.method: Read the Known Issues section of the official v1.3.0rc23 release note and preserved its model, precision, scheduler, parallelism and GPU conditions. No failure was reproduced.

sources.limitations: The project reports its own known issues; occurrence rate, affected range and fixes were not independently verified.

limitations: The article does not claim every listed issue occurs in every matching deployment.
Absence from the list is not evidence that another configuration is safe.
No GPU, model weight or multi-node environment was available for reproduction.
conflict_of_interest: NVIDIA selects and describes known issues for its own release candidate.
recheck_triggers: A follow-up RC or stable release marks an issue fixed
Independent runtime reports reproduce or contradict the disclosure
